newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade publications show stable sales.
newsitem.headline: German trade publications show stable sales.

text.p: German trade publications maintained stable turnover and circulation in 1996 and foresee steady growth for the current year, their main industry association said on Monday.

With nearly 3,500 titles and 513 million issues distributed annually, trade publications made a total 3.9 billion marks last year -- more than half of which came from advertising sales, the German Trade Press Association said.

It was not possible to directly compare figures from 1996 and 1995 because this was the first year that a private organisation, market research institute Emnid, had provided the data, association spokesman Klaus Kottmeier said.
Industry data had previously come directly from the government statistics office.
The value of trade publications for advertisers has been consistently underestimated by the periodical industry, Kottmeier said.
"These figures demonstrate that the trade publication industry occupies a vital role for advertisers that until now was not fully recognised," he said.

The number of trade periodicals rose for the first time since 1993 with 250 new titles appearing on the market and 100 folding. Particular expansion occurred among technical publications like those for the building industry, he said.

Kottmeier said the importance of business abroad had increased last year, with nearly a fourth of all German trade publishers working with foreign partners and about the same number producing foreign language titles in Germany.
Twenty-one percent of the most profitable publishing houses have foreign units or shares in companies abroad.

Kottmeier said the figures referred to income from trade publications. Finance publications, hobby magazines, trade books, electronic books, services and printing house publications were excluded, he said.
The Association of the German Trade Press has 700 member publications, representing 35,000 employees.
